claims.text: The Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy initially contains a non-equilibrium, metastable solid solution.
Aging at high temperature in a controlled atmosphere causes intermetallic compounds to precipitate from the solid solution.
Intermetallic precipitation transforms the alloy from its metastable state toward a more stable state.
The formation of intermetallic compounds changes the alloy's corrosion resistance.
The formation of intermetallic compounds changes the alloy's high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Whether corrosion resistance is retained or lost depends on the type and distribution of the intermetallic compounds.
Whether high-temperature oxidation resistance is retained or lost depends on the type and distribution of the intermetallic compounds.
Intermetallic precipitation is governed by temperature and time boundaries.
Data on transformation pathways and kinetics in Mg-containing high-entropy alloys are limited.
A controlled comparison of aged and unaged samples is proposed.
The hypothesis is falsified if aging produces no significant difference in either microstructure or corrosion and high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to unaged samples.
